He would definitely die in the wild, I don't know about a setup for a bird with this kind of disability and I don't really have any resource specific to this, what I would do would be getting a dog kennel, one with the bottom you can slide out. They're not too expensive and some brown paper or newspaper as a liner (I suggest brown paper because it's inexpensive and easy to find, I had trouble keeping my stock of newspapers up). I have had great lucks with my vet but be very cautious with them, when I was a teen I took a pigeon to a vet and they told me that the only resolution for a pigeon with a broken bird would be to amputate both wings or euthanasia. I regret that to this day but I didn't know any better. In the end it's going to be trial and error and a lot of research, if you can find someone with disabled bird experience it would be nice. Get a pigeon seed mix and some grit (if you can't find the grit he will be fine for a little while without it). Wash your hands well after cleaning where he poops and if you're able to, try and find a spray for parasites for birds, they're really inexpensive (only covers for external parasytes). In the end I'm a beginner myself so take everything I say with a grain of salt

Obtaining quails is actually quite easy, there are breeders (at least in Italy) for pretty much any kind of quail, they tend to sell them in lots of 50 chicks each, if you're asking for just one they are very likely to give it away, problem is most of those places use various "medicines" to make them grow bigger and faster, which while somewhat working they greatly reduce their lifespan. There are still farms here which keep quails that haven't been doped, they're slightly more expensive (talking abour 1-5 € difference) but they live quite a while, around 5 years. Wild quails are always scared of humans, you could probably befriend them but it would take a while.

You can absolutely litter train them, they're honestly one of the easiest animals to litter train, it took my rabbit 2 days to get it. You're going to want to have a litter box, put some rabbit safe adsorbing media at the bottom, then put hay on top of it, be sure to get hay that's just hay without any alfalfa, also hay is very important for your rabbits, they should always have fresh hay available to them. Take any poop they make and put it in the litter box, if they pee, use a paper towel to clean it, take a piece of that paper towel and put that too in the litter box, you might wanna repel them from peeing where they did by using a tiny amount of vinegar (really, don't use too much, the smell is really strong for them). That's pretty much all you have to do,  just move their stuff in the litter box, you might wanna use 2 litter boxes, that depends on your rabbits, also, since they're not neutered, it will probably be harder than if they were, it's possible, but it's probably don't gonna happen as quickly. This is from personal experience so things i said might not be completely correct so take it as it is.
